notes: Each entry was verified by reading the unmodified v15.0.0 source. Line numbers point at the exact statement that introduces the vulnerability. CWE IDs reflect what static analyzers would reasonably emit for that pattern, not just the canonical OWASP description.

vulnerabilities.description: User-controlled `q` parameter interpolated directly into a raw `sequelize.query` SQL string in product search.
Login endpoint builds a raw SQL query from `req.body.email` via template literal; classic auth-bypass SQL injection.
`res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file))` joins user input with the upload directory without canonicalization, allowing path traversal.
RSA private key for JWT signing is hardcoded as a string constant. (Semgrep flags the related HMAC and key-store secrets nearby, not this exact line; useful blind-spot example for the report.)
HMAC secret `'pa4qacea4VK9t9nGv7yZtwmj'` is hardcoded into the source.
MD5 used for the `hash()` helper that backs password hashing in legacy flows.
`vm.runInContext('safeEval(orderLinesData)', sandbox)` evaluates user-supplied YAML/JSON via the unmaintained `notevil` package, allowing RCE.
`res.redirect(toUrl)` accepts an arbitrary URL from the `?to=` query parameter, mitigated only by a stale allowlist.
`eval(expression)` is used to compute the CAPTCHA answer; the expression is also derived from `Math.random()`, making it predictable as well.
`request.get(url)` fetches an arbitrary remote URL from `req.body.imageUrl` with no allowlist, allowing SSRF into internal hosts.
XML upload calls `libxml.parseXml(data, { noent: true })`, leaving external-entity expansion enabled (XXE).
`pug.compile(template)` compiles a template constructed from user-controlled `username`, enabling server-side template injection.
